Hypotheses: Real L in R3, Q=A sum Li^2+(2A+4C) sum LiLj with A=5/48 and the ADR 0024 adjudicated C.
Scope: Exact real quadratic-polynomial consequence of existing fourth-order assembly. Not a full Hamiltonian or all-orders coercivity theorem.
Support CHK:review-derived-coercivity-and-multichann-8dd636:assembled-q4-has-the-corrected-sharp-coe-c84029: Exact symbolic polynomial identity, rational coefficients and full 3 by 3 eigenspectrum; no physical all-orders implication.
statement: For real L, the adjudicated Q4 equals d||L||^2+e(sum L_i)^2 with d=13035490122347/275331901291200>0 and e=15644916262153/275331901291200>0. Its sharp lower and upper coefficients are d and 29985119454403/137665950645600; the assembled cross coefficient is the historical one plus 25/256.

Hypotheses: Finite nonempty decay/error families: p_j>=0, m_j>0, ell_l>=0, s>=0, P_j=p_j+2s>0 and R_l=r_l-2s>0.; Positive cutoff-independent bound coefficients, 0<a_n<1 tending to zero and |alpha_n|>=c_alpha a_n^s.; Raw bound M1 is available at selected physical times c log(1/a_n); optional horizon c<=h has h>0.; Spectral consequences additionally require actual norm approximation and MT2 measure/totality or compatible-history-kernel hypotheses.
Scope: Analytic finite-family optimization with source normalization, time amplification and physical horizon. Extends MT4; a nonpositive bound means no positive guarantee. Actual Wilson and continuum-kernel inputs remain open.
Support CHK:review-derived-coercivity-and-multichann-8dd636:multichannel-target-intervals-yield-ever-df0588: Exact cross-multiplication, pair intersection and single-plateau specialization identities.
Support CHK:review-derived-coercivity-and-multichann-8dd636:multichannel-optimum-respects-all-errors-3ad24b: Finite rational multi-term, horizon, amplification and zero-margin cases, not a proof of Wilson estimates.
statement: For raw terms A_j a^-p_j exp(-m_j t) and B_l a^r_l exp(ell_l t) with squared-source normalization a^-2s, the sharp positive logarithmic-time guarantee is min_jl (R_l m_j-P_j ell_l)/(P_j+R_l), capped by min_j(m_j-P_j/h). A target 0<M<min m_j is admissible iff max_j P_j/(m_j-M)<=min_l R_l/(M+ell_l) and <=h; its lower time endpoint is a witness.

Hypotheses: Finite nonempty decay/error families: p_j>=0, m_j>0, ell_l>=0, s>=0, P_j=p_j+2s>0 and R_l=r_l-2s>0.; Positive cutoff-independent bound coefficients, 0<a_n<1 tending to zero and |alpha_n|>=c_alpha a_n^s.; Raw bound M1 is available at selected physical times c log(1/a_n); optional horizon c<=h has h>0.; Spectral consequences additionally require actual norm approximation and MT2 measure/totality or compatible-history-kernel hypotheses.; For examples, the bound holds throughout the available horizon, the coefficients can be chosen once, and the target has unit norm.
Scope: Sharpness among abstract positive spectral models satisfying the budget. Not a counterexample to Wilson Yang-Mills or a supplied Wilson estimate.
Support CHK:review-derived-coercivity-and-multichann-8dd636:multichannel-sharpness-retains-the-exact-d717c8: Exact weighted-product and horizon exponents and 16 rational one-atom examples. AM-GM and limiting sharpness remain analytic.
statement: One positive-energy atom saturates each binding pair or horizon rate of the multichannel budget. A nonpositive binding constraint permits a centered zero-energy atom. Two-point exponential probes realize the same sharp exponents for s>0 after a cutoff-independent prefactor enlargement.
